CLASS 23 · THE MUSIC ROOM

Welcome to the Music Room.

The third room of the school, beside the Library and the School Garden: instruments on the shelves, the words music uses on the wall, and the people — solo, duet, band, chorus, conductor, singer, orchestra — who fill the room with sound. Every card is right here with a download button and one game to play tonight.

THE INSTRUMENT SHELF

Thirty-three instruments, from accordion to xylophone.

Everything on the room’s shelves, one card each: strings you bow, keys you press, drums you boom and the small ones you shake, click and squeeze. Every instrument’s lesson is right here — what it is, how it makes its sound and how to build a home version tonight.

THE WORDS ON THE WALL

Thirteen music words, from beat to volume.

The words music uses every day — beat, tempo, melody, pitch, volume — each one on its own card with its lesson right here: the meaning in child-size words, where to hear it and a game to play it. Learn the words and every song you meet gets easier to talk about.

WHO’S IN THE ROOM

Seven ways people make music together.

The singer who goes first, the duet that shares, the band that divides, the chorus that joins in, the conductor who leads with a stick, the solo that takes the spotlight and the orchestra that is all of it at once — seven cards about making music with other people, each with its lesson right here.

All fifty-three cards live in the Music Room flashcard set — every card page has a download button with the full-size image. The room sits on the Learning Path as Class 23, and the instruments also browse from the shelves of the School Library.

TEACHER’S LESSON

How this class is taught.

By the end of this class: your child has met all 53 cards in Music Room, said each word with you and tried one small activity from the lesson.

  1. 01
    Welcome

    “Hello! Today we are learning about Music Room. We have 53 cards, and we will look at them one at a time.”

    How: Sit side by side with the cards in front of you. Keep your voice warm and unhurried, and let your child touch the cards.

  2. Cards 1–10
  3. 02
    Card 1 · Accordion

    “Squeeze it out, push it in — eee-ahh, eee-ahh! The accordion sings when it breathes, just like you do.”

    How: Stand up, hold an imaginary accordion and pump your arms while you hum one long note — big arms out, small arms in. Pump faster and hear your hum speed up, just like real bellows.

  4. 03
    Card 2 · Bagpipes

    “Fill the bag with air and squeeze — a long, loud, droning nyeee-ahhh that never stops for breath.”

    How: Blow up a paper bag, hold it shut and squeeze slowly while you hum — a two-second bagpipe. Then squeeze faster for a silly, stuttering version and let the giggles tune themselves.

  5. 04
    Card 3 · Banjo

    “Pling-pling-pling! The banjo twangs like a rubber band on a biscuit tin — bright, bouncy and quick.”

    How: Stretch a rubber band over an empty tub and pluck it short and long — a one-string banjo. Pluck near the edge for a high pling, near the middle for a low one, and count your strings of tins.

  6. 05
    Card 4 · Bass Drum

    “BOOM… BOOM… BOOM. Slow and huge — the bass drum is the floor of the music.”

    How: Pat the floor on every BOOM while a march plays — pat, step, pat, step. Then swap: stamp on the boom, pat on the quiet. Your living room is now a parade.

  7. 06
    Card 5 · Bells

    “Plink… plink… plink! Little bells say one clean note each — ding goes every single one.”

    How: Line up three cups upside down and tap them with a spoon — one high, one middle, one low if you can. Play a three-note bell song of your own and ring it twice.

  8. 07
    Card 6 · Castanets

    “Click-click-clickity-click! Castanets talk with their mouths shut — the fastest chatter in the room.”

    How: Click a rhythm with your tongue against the roof of your mouth — click-click… click! Hands free castanets. Then click fast like a spider, slow like a snail, and ask which is which.

  9. 08
    Card 7 · Cello

    “Mmmmmm — low and warm, like a big dog humming. The cello sings with a bow instead of a mouth.”

    How: Hum your lowest mmmmm and rub one hand up your other arm like a bow — long and smooth. Big slow arm, low slow hum: that is cello breathing, and it works on grown-ups too.

  10. 09
    Card 8 · Clarinet

    “Whooooo — wobbly and smooth, like blowing across a bottle with a straw. The clarinet giggles when it plays high.”

    How: Blow across the top of an empty bottle — wh0000! That airy hoot is a bottle clarinet. Fill it with a little water and the note climbs higher: your clarinet just grew shorter.

  11. 10
    Card 9 · Cymbals

    “CRASH! …sssssssss… One hit and a long, sparkly tail — cymbals are the fireworks of the band.”

    How: Crash your hands together high in the air, then let them sink slowly to the floor while your voice goes sssssss — the crash getting smaller. Big crash, tiny crash, and one crash with a yawn.

  12. 11
    Card 10 · Drum Kit

    “Boom-tsh, boom-boom-tsh! The drum kit is four rhythms at the same time — feet and hands, all talking together.”

    How: Sit on a chair: pat your knees for the toms, stamp one foot for the bass boom, clap for the tsh. Now put them together — boom, clap, knees-knees — and you are a kit.

  13. Cards 11–20
  14. 12
    Card 11 · Drum

    “Boom boom boom-boom-boom! The drum says what your heart says — tap it and it answers back.”

    How: Pat your knees — boom. Pat a cushion — boom. Pat the sofa arm — boooooom. Play a drum tour of the house and rate each surface: bouncy boom, flat tap or forbidden bell.

  15. 13
    Card 12 · Flute

    “Whooooo-ooo! Light and airy, like blowing over a bottle’s mouth — the flute is breath turned into birdsong.”

    How: Hold an empty bottle and blow gently across its mouth until it sings — that is exactly how a flute works. Now try short hoots, a long swoop, and a bottle lullaby of three notes.

  16. 14
    Card 13 · French Horn

    “Mwooooah — long and golden, like a voice singing through a seashell. The horn calls across mountains.”

    How: Curl your hands around your mouth like a horn bell and call mwoooah across the room. Answer each other back and forth — one call each, waiting for the echo. That is a horn conversation.

  17. 15
    Card 14 · Gong

    “GOOOOOOOONG… one hit, and the sound keeps travelling like ripples on a pond.”

    How: Strike an imaginary gong, then freeze and listen until your invisible sound completely disappears — count how long it lasts. Quiet game champion gets tomorrow’s first mallet.

  18. 16
    Card 15 · Guitar

    “Strum-strum-strum! The guitar hums when you brush all its strings at once — like petting a cat that sings.”

    How: Stretch rubber bands of different thicknesses over a shoebox with a hole cut in the lid — a box guitar. Pluck each band: thick string low, thin string high. Line up three and play a chord.

  19. 17
    Card 16 · Harmonica

    “Hoo-hooo — hiiin! Blow a note, breathe back a note. The harmonica turns breathing into a tune.”

    How: Hum a note out through pursed lips, then breathe the same note back in — hooo-iii. Do it four times slowly: that is a harmonica warm-up, and it doubles as settling-down magic.

  20. 18
    Card 17 · Harp

    “Plink… plinnnng… and whoosh up all the strings — the harp does sparkles better than anybody.”

    How: Stretch several rubber bands across a baking tray — short ones and long ones. Plink each: short band high, long band low. Now sweep a thumb across them all — home glissando.

  21. 19
    Card 18 · Maracas

    “Chik-chik-chiki-chik! The maracas rattle like seeds dancing in a pod — one shake, two shake, shake-shake-shake.”

    How: Fill a bottle with a spoonful of rice, screw the lid tight and shake: chik! Two bottles, one per hand. Now shake only when the music is loud and freeze when it goes quiet.

  22. 20
    Card 19 · Microphone

    “La-la-LAAAA! Sing into your fist-microphone and let it grow your voice as big as a garden.”

    How: Hold a hairbrush or wooden spoon as your mic and announce something wonderful: “Good evening! Tonight we will eat spaghetti!” Then pass the mic — every person gets one announcement.

  23. 21
    Card 20 · Stage Microphone

    “One-two, one-two! Tapping the mic gently and saying one-two is how every show begins — testing, testing!”

    How: Compare the two microphone cards side by side: what is the same, what is different? Then stage a show — one mic for the singer, one for the announcer, and one-two-one-two to open.

  24. Cards 21–30
  25. 22
    Card 21 · Oboe

    “Nasally neee-nah — a bit like a happy duck with excellent manners. The oboe quacks beautifully.”

    How: Fold a strip of paper in half, hold the folded end between your thumbs and blow — a grass reed quacks like an oboe. If it honks, congratulations: you are holding a real reed principle.

  26. 23
    Card 22 · Piano

    “Plink plink plonk! Walk your fingers up the keys — the further right you go, the smaller the mouse squeaks.”

    How: Draw eight paper keys on a strip, tape it to a table and play with one finger: middle C, then a step right, then a run home. Squeeze the sponge — the louder the piano, the squishier the play.

  27. 24
    Card 23 · Piccolo

    “Fweeee! Sharp and sparkly, like a whistle that learned music. You will hear the piccolo over everyone.”

    How: Sing a note as high as you can — your piccolo voice. Now your lowest — your tuba voice. Play high-low-high-low with your hands marking up and down, and let a sibling call the shots.

  28. 25
    Card 24 · Recorder

    “Whoooo — clean and simple, like a bird whistle with a straight face. Gentle breath, pretty note.”

    How: Cover the holes with a toilet-roll tube and hum through it — a pretend recorder. Real one? Blow SOFTLY with the thumb hole covered for low notes, open for high, and brace for Hot Cross Buns.

  29. 26
    Card 25 · Saxophone

    “Wah-wah-wahhhoo! Smooth and bendy, like a voice made of brass. The saxophone slides between notes on purpose.”

    How: Sing aaaa and swoop up into it from underneath — waaaa-AAA. That bend is saxophone breathing. Do three: a sleepy bend, a surprised bend and a bend that answers the question “dinner?”

  30. 27
    Card 26 · Sitar

    “Bzzziiiing — a plink that shivers! The sitar’s strings buzz like a happy bee with a melody.”

    How: Hum one note while wiggling it up and down — oooo-WII-oooo. That wobble is what a sitar does to every note. Then sing a tiny tune entirely in wiggles and vote on the best one.

  31. 28
    Card 27 · Tambourine

    “Tap-shake-shake! The tambourine says boom with its face and jingle-jangle with its edges.”

    How: Slap the card on your knee — tap! Then shake it in the air — jangle! Play tap-tap-SHAKE, tap-tap-SHAKE, and end with the tambourine held high for one long overhead rattle. Encore rules apply.

  32. 29
    Card 28 · Trombone

    “Wahhh-wOOO-wahhh! The trombone slides like a cartoon voice — down for sleepy, up for surprised.”

    How: One arm is the slide: push it out while your voice sinks — wahhhh — pull it in while your voice climbs — woo! Play three slides: giant yawn down, rocket up, and a slow wobble in the middle.

  33. 30
    Card 29 · Trumpet

    “Ta-da-ta-DAAA! Bright and royal — the trumpet is the fanfare machine of the Music Room.”

    How: Buzz a raspberry into your fist, then pull the fist away slowly — the buzz thins into a trumpet-ish brrrap. Now add three royal notes: ta-ta-ta-DAAA, and bow. Applause is mandatory.

  34. 31
    Card 30 · Tuba

    “Bwommm… bwom-bwommm! Deep as a basement, warm as soup — the tuba sings the floor of the music.”

    How: Sing your lowest possible note with a hand on your throat to feel the buzz — your inner tuba. Now walk in slow motion while humming it: tuba steps. Fast motion is strictly piccolo-only.

  35. Cards 31–40
  36. 32
    Card 31 · Ukulele

    “Plinky-plink! Bright and light as a coconut falling on sand — the ukulele only knows happy songs.”

    How: Four strings, four fingers: trace a ukulele on paper, tape it to a table and strum the air strings with a thumb sweep. Sing any song while strumming — the uke rule is singing comes first.

  37. 33
    Card 32 · Violin

    “Eeeeee-ahh — high and sweet, sometimes a purr, sometimes a cry. The violin sings while you stroke it.”

    How: Arm bow, table violin: stroke one arm slowly with the other while singing aaaa — long bow, long note. Short bows for a running mouse song, long bows for a sleepy moon song. Bow changes tell all.

  38. 34
    Card 33 · Xylophone

    “Bonk-bonk-binki-bonk! Wooden bars talk in colours — big bar low, little bar high, run down the rainbow.”

    How: Line up drinking glasses filled with different water amounts and tap them with a spoon — more water, lower bonk. Order your glass band from biggest bonk to tiniest and play the rain song.

  39. 35
    Card 34 · Beat

    “Tap-tap-tap-tap! The beat is the steady one — not fast, not slow, just always there, like a heart that learned music.”

    How: Play a steady tap on your knees — tap-tap-tap — and walk around the room exactly on it. Then tap the beat while a song plays: did your taps and the song agree? If yes, you found it.

  40. 36
    Card 35 · Clap

    “CLAP! One clap says hello, two claps say again, and a clap-pattern says: your turn now.”

    How: Play the clap-echo game: you clap a pattern — clap, clap-clap, clap — and your child claps it back exactly. Then swap leader. Three rounds is a full music lesson; applause after is automatic.

  41. 37
    Card 36 · Dance

    “Step-step-spin! When the music plays and your feet join in — that is dancing, and nobody does it wrong.”

    How: Play freeze dance: music on means dance any way you like, music off means statue. Fast song = fast dance, slow song = slow-motion dance. Three songs and everyone is happily exhausted.

  42. 38
    Card 37 · Harmony

    “One note is you, one note is me — sing both together and… ahhh! That cozy together-sound is harmony.”

    How: You sing one long note — aaaa. Your child sings another long note at the same time. Listen together: do they fit, or argue? Try again until you find the fit — that agreement is harmony.

  43. 39
    Card 38 · Listen

    “Ears open, voices off… What do you hear? Listening is the game where quiet wins.”

    How: Play the listening minute: everyone closes eyes for sixty quiet seconds and collects sounds — a fridge hum, a bird, a car, your own breath. Count your finds together and crown the rarest one.

  44. 40
    Card 39 · Lyrics

    “The song says words! Sing the tune, then say what it SAYS — the lyrics are the song’s talking part.”

    How: Sing a favourite song, then ask: what did the song SAY? Let your child tell the story of the lyrics in their own talking voice — then swap: turn a bedtime instruction into song lyrics and sing it.

  45. 41
    Card 40 · Melody

    “La-la-la-LA! The melody is the tune — the part you hum in the bath and whistle on the stairs.”

    How: Hum a tiny melody of three notes — la-la-LA — and have your child echo it. Then ask: did it go up at the end or down? Draw it in the air with a finger: up, down, or flat? Melody becomes visible.

  46. Cards 41–50
  47. 42
    Card 41 · Music

    “This whole card set IS music — singing, drums, bells, dancing. Say the big word slowly: muuu-sic.”

    How: Play the music-or-not game: hum a tune (music!), bang a door (just a door!), sing while washing hands (music!). Let your child be the judge and keep score — the arguments are the curriculum.

  48. 43
    Card 42 · Pitch

    “High like a bird — eeee! Low like a bear — mmmm. Pitch is how high or how low the sound sits.”

    How: Hold both hands out: high hands = sing eeee (bird), low hands = sing mmmm (bear). Now play the pitch ladder — hand rises, voice rises; hand sinks, voice sinks. Speed up until someone giggles.

  49. 44
    Card 43 · Song

    “Words plus tune equals a song! Sing any song you love — a song is music that knows what it wants to say.”

    How: Make a two-line song right now about whatever is in front of you — the dog, the rain, the dinner. Sing it twice. Add a chorus of one word. That is a real song and it belongs to its writer.

  50. 45
    Card 44 · Tempo

    “Slow like a snail… fast like a puppy! Tempo is the speed of the beat — and you are the dial.”

    How: March to a hand-clapped beat: slow tempo, snail parade. Now the same march at puppy tempo. Now YOU clap and I march — the clapper is the tempo boss. Swap jobs after three songs.

  51. 46
    Card 45 · Tune

    “You know that song in your head right now? THAT is a tune. Hum yours out loud — tunes want out.”

    How: Play the tune hunt: hum a famous tune — Happy Birthday — and have your child name it. Then swap: they hum, you guess. End by inventing one brand-new family tune and naming it after the day.

  52. 47
    Card 46 · Volume

    “Whisper-small… and then HUGE! Volume is how loud the sound is — and the dial is yours to turn.”

    How: Sing one song at four volumes: whisper, inside voice, outside voice, and — quietly — giant. Walk the dial up and down on request. Freeze at whisper level: the hardest and funniest setting.

  53. 48
    Card 47 · Band

    “One-two-three-four! A band is friends playing together — everybody different, everybody on the same beat.”

    How: Form a family band right now: pot-lid cymbals, jar maracas, box guitar, spoon mic. Choose a song everyone knows, count one-two-three-four and play it. Rule one: every instrument gets heard.

  54. 49
    Card 48 · Chorus

    “Everybody now — a chorus is ALL of us singing! Many voices, one song, twice the joy.”

    How: Be a two-person chorus: sing any song you both know, together, at the same time. Then add the whole family at dinner — the chorus grows one person per meal until the neighbours join.

  55. 50
    Card 49 · Conductor

    “Whoosh-whoosh! The conductor waves the beat — big waves for loud, tiny waves for quiet, and a fist means STOP.”

    How: Hand someone a wooden spoon — the baton. They wave slow, the family sings slow; big waves mean loud, fingers-closed means freeze. Everyone conducts one song. Sunset finale required.

  56. 51
    Card 50 · Duet

    “Just us two — you start, I join! A duet is two people and one song, taking turns and then together.”

    How: Play a kitchen duet: one person keeps the beat on knees, the other hums the tune. Swap roles after one verse. Golden rule — the beat-keeper is the boss, and the boss must be steady.

  57. Cards 51–53
  58. 52
    Card 51 · Orchestra

    “The orchestra is a whole city of instruments! Strings here, drums there — a hundred friends, one enormous song.”

    How: Seat your toys in sections — stuffed animals on strings duty, blocks on percussion. Conduct with the wooden spoon, cue each family in turn, and end with the whole toy orchestra at once.

  59. 53
    Card 52 · Singer

    “La-la-LAAA — the singer leads with their voice! Your mouth is the instrument, and it never leaves home.”

    How: Everyone picks one line of a known song and sings it solo — one line each, pass the song around the table. Applaud every single voice. That is a recital, and snacks are traditional.

  60. 54
    Card 53 · Solo

    “All eyes on ONE — a solo is you and the song, everybody else listening. Deep breath… and go!”

    How: Solo time: each person plays or sings something short by themselves while everyone else is audience — then serious applause and one compliment each. The solo slot is sacred; keep it short.

  61. 55
    Practice

    “Now you are the teacher! Pick any card and tell me what it is.”

    How: Let your child choose the card and say the word in their own way. Teaching someone else is the strongest way to remember.

  62. 56
    Check

    “Can you find Accordion? Now show me Tambourine.”

    How: A point, a fetch or the word all count as a pass. If they are unsure, name it for them and try again another day — there are no scores and no pressure.

  63. 57
    Well done

    “Well done! Today we met 53 cards. Let us look for one of them at home.”

    How: End on a win, then spot one of the words in real life today. Meeting it again in the real world is what makes it stay.

Read the script while you show the cards — the say-lines are yours to say out loud and the how-lines are the activity behind each step. Skip, shorten or repeat anything: the class bends to your child, never the other way round.
